<!-- All news items below this line -->
;Business and economy
*[[Economy of the United Kingdom]]
**[[House of Fraser]] announces that it intends to close 31 of its 59 stores, including its flagship store on [[London|London's]] [[Oxford Street]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-44394948 (BBC)]
*[[Lender of last resort]]
**[[Argentina]] agrees with [[International Monetary Fund|IMF]] negotiators on a [[United States dollar|US$]]50 billion loan. [http://amp.kansascity.com/news/business/national-international/article212781164.html (AP via ''The Kansas City Star'')]
*[[IKEA]] announces that it plans to phase out [[single-use ]]plastic items by [[2020]], and intends to move toward [[sustainability]] in its product design. [https://www.bbc.com/news/business-44398356 (BBC)]

;International relations
*[[Japan–United States relations]]
**[[Donald Trump]] and [[Shinzō Abe]] discuss improving trade relations between the two countries. [https://www.straitstimes.com/asia/east-asia/trump-says-working-with-shinzo-abe-to-improve-us-japan-trade-relations (''The Straits Times'')]
*[[2018 North Korea–United States summit]], [[North Korea–United States relations]]
**[[Donald Trump]] says that he might invite [[North Korea]]n leader [[Kim Jong-un]] to the [[United States]] if the planned summit meeting in [[Singapore]] goes well. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-44406498 (BBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[Abortion in the United Kingdom]]
**The [[Supreme Court of the United Kingdom|Supreme Court]] of the [[UK]] dismisses a legal challenge by the [[Northern Ireland Human Rights Commission]] of the restrictive [[Northern Ireland]] [[abortion law]]s, as the court has no jurisdiction in this specific case. Four of seven judges note that these laws are incompatible with the [[European Convention on Human Rights]] "in prohibiting abortion in cases of rape and incest and fatal [[fetus|foetal]] abnormality", a matter of right to respect for private and family life guaranteed by the Convention. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2018/jun/07/supreme-court-dismisses-bid-to-overturn-northern-ireland-abortion-laws (''The Guardian'')]
*[[2018 North Korea–United States summit]], [[North Korea–Singapore relations]]
**Two [[South Korea]]n media personnel from [[Korean Broadcasting System|KBS News]] are arrested for trespassing the home of a [[North Korea]]n envoy in Singapore. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/news/singapore/south-korean-media-kbs-arrested-trespass-north-korea-embassador-10408134 (Channel NewsAsia)]
*[[Canada|Canadian]] prime minister [[Justin Trudeau]] is accused of groping a journalist in 2000. He denies he made negative interactions. [http://thehill.com/policy/international/391298-trudeau-denies-negative-interactions-after-editorial-resurfaces-alleging (''The Hill'')]

;Politics and elections
*[[2018 Ontario general election]]
**[[Canada|Canadian]] citizens residing in [[Ontario]] go to the polls to elect a new [[Legislative Assembly of Ontario|provincial government]]. [https://www.ctvnews.ca/canada/ontario-could-see-a-seismic-political-shift-in-today-s-provincial-election-1.3962929 (CTV)]
**The [[Progressive Conservative Party of Ontario|Progressive Conservative Party]] of [[Doug Ford Jr.|Doug Ford]] wins a sweeping victory, ending 15 years of [[Ontario Liberal Party|Liberal Party]] rule in the province. The Liberal Party becomes a minority party (or third party) for the first time since its foundation and later [[1867 Ontario general election|first provincial election]], has losing official party status. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-canada-election-ontario/populist-doug-ford-set-to-win-ontario-polls-promises-prosperity-idUSKCN1J318K (Reuters)] [http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/toronto/if-ontario-liberals-lose-recognized-party-status-after-thursday-s-election-what-comes-next-1.4693261 (CBC.ca)]
**[[Ontario New Democratic Party]] wins 40 seats, becoming [[Leader of the Opposition (Ontario)|Official Opposition]] for the first time since the [[1987 Ontario general election|1987 election]]. [https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-ontario-ndp-pick-up-big-gains-in-provincial-election-will-form/ (''The Global and Mail'')]
**[[Ontario Green Party]] has their first ever MPP elected. [[Mike Schreiner]] is elected in [[Guelph (provincial electoral district)|Guelph district]] in southwestern Ontario. [http://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/kitchener-waterloo/ontario-election-results-guelph-1.4695857 (CBC.ca)]
*[[Spain|Spanish]] [[King of Spain|King]] [[Felipe VI]] swears in the [[Sánchez I Government|cabinet]] of [[Prime Minister of Spain|Prime Minister]] [[Pedro Sánchez]]. It is the first cabinet in European history, and the only in the world, to be composed primarily of women. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-44382051 (BBC)]

;Science and technology
*[[Life on Mars]]
**[[NASA]] announces the discovery of preserved [[organic matter]] in an ancient lake bed on [[Mars]] by its [[Curiosity (rover)|Curiosity rover]]. It has not been determined if the matter was potentially related to past life on Mars or not. [https://www.theguardian.com/science/2018/jun/07/nasa-mars-rover-finds-organic-matter-in-ancient-lake-bed (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Facebook]] reports an error in privacy settings that has affected 14 million users. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-44407767 (BBC)]

;Sports
*[[Corruption in Ghana]]
**[[Ghana]]ian Minister of Information [[Mustapha Abdul-Hamid]] announces the decision to dissolve the [[Ghana Football Association]] following the publication of an exposé of the organisation by [[Anas Aremeyaw Anas]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/uk-soccer-ghana-corruption/ghana-to-dissolve-football-association-over-bribery-allegations-idUKKCN1J32NI (Reuters)]
*[[2018 Stanley Cup Finals]]
**In [[ice hockey]], the [[Washington Capitals]] win their first [[Stanley Cup]] after defeating the [[Vegas Golden Knights]] 4–1 in the finals. [http://www.sportingnews.com/nhl/news/stanley-cup-final-2018-vegas-golden-knights-washington-capitals-game-5-live-score-result-updates-video-highlights/1ee8ocmkuwny316l38l6jr67yf (''Sporting News'')]
